main_text.p: præficarumque & aliorum ad id con-duƈtorum ejulatus, ritusque pudendos ac indecoros sustulit. Ad hæc artificia omnis generis, quæ honesta & utilia, civitati commendavit, iisque honorem tribuit, ac in usum deduxit: legemque statuit ne filius, qui à patre nullam artem accepisset, eundem patrem alere, quod alioqui eum facere oportebat, teneretur. Quin & Areopagitis præcepit, ut otiosos ac inertes corriperent, & pœnis quoque afficerent. Inertiam enim civium pestem civitatis esse putavit. Natos ex meretricibus à necessitate alendi parentes liberos esse voluit. [illegible, ~2 letters]Mœchos in facinore deprehensos occi-[illegible, ~2 letters]dere deprehendentibus permisit. Sed raptus reos multo, quàm decuit, le-nior fuit, ut & in eos qui virgines vio-lent. [illegible, ~3 letters]Ius vendendi filias & sorores, nisi in crimine deprehensas, abrogavit. [illegible, ~1 letter]Præmia Olympionicis drachmas D; iis, qui Isthmia vicissent, drachmas c, ho-noris causa statuit. [illegible, ~2 letters]Ex agri Attici fru-ctibus exportari quicquam vetuit præ-ter oleum: aliter facientes c drachma-rum multam solvere ærario jussit. [illegible, ~1 letter]Multa alia quoque fanciit [?]: quorum nihil memorabilius quàm hoc, quòd honoribus privavit eos, qui exortà for-[illegible, ~1 letter]ditione neutri factioni [?] se junge-rent,

page.notes: Long s has been written as plain s throughout. Printed small curved marks stand after "quoque", "quorum" and "solvere"; they are not letters and are not reproduced. "fanciit" and "factioni" are uncertain and marked [?]. "vicissent" has a mark over the i that may be a printer's accent. Left margin notes are cut off at the scan edge and mostly unreadable, so each is marked illegible with an estimated letter count; their placement is approximate. Bottom edge: small marks and numerals (possibly a signature) are too faint to read, so none are transcribed. The paragraph continues on the next page.
